_note: Real captured Claude responses to the 6 custom slash commands (Ep 11 b-roll content). Captured 2026-08-11 via the actual command prompts on self-contained examples. These are the authentic on-screen proof — do NOT edit the responses; they are real model output.

commands.one_liner: Assume it already failed. Find out why.
commands.arg: launching my $9/mo email-summary Chrome extension on Product Hunt next month
response: Dead by month 4 — 11 paying users, killed the Stripe account.
Cause: Gmail ships free thread-summaries the week you launch.
Warning we ignore: 300 PH upvotes, only 4 convert to paid.
2k followers ≠ buyers — that's peers, not inbox-drowning execs.
Fix today: presell 15 annual seats before Product Hunt.

commands.arg: quitting my job to go full-time on my 800-subscriber, $0-revenue newsletter
response: Stable paycheck → assumption, not fact — runway math undone.
800 free, $0 revenue: you haven't tested if they'll pay.
Not modeled: family whose risk tolerance you never surveyed.
Second-order: no salary kills the 'just for fun' spell.
Outsider's read: quitting a job to keep a hobby.

commands.arg: we should rewrite our Python monolith in Rust for performance
response: Your monolith idles on API calls, not CPU — Rust won't help.
3-year-old code hides edge cases a rewrite silently drops.
A rewrite ships nothing for months while revenue waits.
Same logic that killed 'templated': effort, no payoff.
Collapses only if profiling proves you're CPU-bound.

commands.one_liner: Maps what to learn before deciding.
commands.arg: adding an AI chatbot to our B2B analytics dashboard
response: Settle it: do users ask 'why', not just 'what'?
Cheap test: Wizard-of-Oz it — human answers, 5 accounts, 2 weeks.
Point of no return: once sales pitches it, ripping it out burns trust.
Hidden cost: per-query LLM spend at scale — margin killer?
Real question: customer pull, or competitor-checkbox reflex?

commands.one_liner: Strips the jargon to expose fuzzy thinking.
commands.arg: our plan to migrate from a monolith to microservices in 6 months
response: Migrating: one big app → many small apps, over 6 months.
Big app = one Lego castle: touch a brick, it all wobbles.
Microservices = separate sets that snap via agreed connectors.
Fuzzy part: you didn't say WHO redraws the connector map.
Like remodeling a house room-by-room while living in it.

commands.one_liner: Builds the strongest case for it.
commands.arg: junior devs should learn to code without AI for their first year
response: Real fluency needs friction — autocomplete skims past gaps.
Debugging your own bugs builds the model AI can't.
Fast wrong answers train bad instincts faster than slow right ones.
You can't judge AI code if you've never written what it replaces.
Strongest point: you can't supervise what you can't do yourself.
